Title: Active learning reduces screening burden in evidence synthesis
Abstract: Title-and-abstract screening is the dominant human cost of a systematic review. We evaluate an active-learning loop in which a classifier is retrained after every batch of reviewer decisions, and report the fraction of records that must be read to reach a fixed recall target across four corpora.

Title: A taxonomy of duplicate detection strategies for bibliographic records
Abstract: Combining exports from several bibliographic databases is error-prone: the same work appears under slightly different titles, with and without a DOI, and with author lists formatted differently. We categorise duplicate-detection strategies by the fields they compare and report precision and recall on a hand-labelled set of record pairs.

Title: Reproducibility of search strategies in published reviews
Abstract: Only a minority of published systematic reviews report a search string that can be re-executed as written. We audit a sample of recent reviews against a minimal reporting checklist and describe the most common omissions.

Title: Snowballing as a complement to database search
Abstract: Backward and forward citation chasing recovers relevant studies that a database search alone does not return. We quantify the additional yield across a set of completed reviews and discuss when the extra effort is justified.
